author: David Reed
summary: chg-25 separates what is checkable from what is judged. PACCA's headline anti-hallucination metric was an LLM's self-reported boolean, from a prompt that labelled keyword constraints as 'hallucination markers'. GC-028 produced the same violation and the same decision across two runs; the judge called it an anti-pattern once and a hallucination the next, flipping the count 0 to 1 with no system change. correct_outcome flipped too.

changes.description: Three-tier evaluator: Tier 1 deterministic keyword checks (whole-word), Tier 2 deterministic outcome and evidence grounding reusing the runtime detector, Tier 3 judge for reasoning quality and fabrication only. Removes the keyword lists from the judge prompt, replaces the single 'hallucinations' counter with three independent ones, and adds a judge stability harness.
changes.failure_pattern: The project's most safety-critical published number moved without the system moving. A deterministic string-containment check was delegated to a nondeterministic judge, and its result was conflated with genuine fabrication under one counter.
changes.root_cause: The judge prompt rendered each case's reasoning_must_not_include list under the header 'Keywords that must NOT appear (hallucination markers)', and the metric was the judge's own self-reported hallucination_detected boolean. correct_outcome was likewise judge-reported.

evidence.note: BASELINE CLAIM: At fa71251 the evaluator performed no Python keyword containment; the check was judge-semantic only, and correct_outcome was judge-self-reported. RESULT: Only lines 359 and 362 (both inside the judge-prompt template) and line 449 correct_outcome=bool(verdict_data.get(...)). No containment check existed in code. (This belongs in a dedicated `baseline` field; the schema addition is spec'd as D6 and awaits a grandfathering decision, so it is recorded here as evidence.)

evidence.source: clinical gate logs, iter-16 vs iter-17 (same GC-028, adjacent HEADs)
evidence.note: Identical system behaviour: AUTO_APPROVED both runs, same criteria cited, accuracy 87.2% (34/39) and an identical failed-case list. The judge scored it 2 ('anti-pattern') then 1 ('hallucination'), flipping the headline count 0 to 1. correct_outcome also flipped True to False.
Returns only the two prompt-template lines, disproving the first implementation's claim that substring matching reproduced an existing Python check. Recorded as AGENT_LESSONS P-013.

Forbidden 'age' under substring also matched coverage, dosage, triage, manage, management, damage, average, stage, usage, percentage, agent, agenda. Across the dataset 'age' fell from 152 hits to 42; 8 of 95 forbidden keywords changed behaviour.
Re-measured the base suite at 940, not the 939 the spec asserted and the executor carried forward unmeasured.

predicted_fixes: constraint_violations, ungrounded_citations and correct_outcome can move only when the system's actual output moves. Verified deterministic with zero variance; the GC-028 flip is impossible for these counters.
GC-046 and GC-048 stop reporting a false constraint violation on rationales containing 'coverage' and 'average'; GC-028 still violates, now for the right reason.
The GC-018/GC-019 sparse-fabrication gate fires when EITHER the judge reports fabrication OR a Tier-1 trap keyword is present, so it no longer rests solely on an LLM boolean.
risk_cases: The first implementation used naive substring matching, justified by a false claim about the base. It would have reported deterministic false positives on GC-028/046/048 for any rationale containing 'coverage', 'dosage' or 'stage' -- common vocabulary in a prior-authorisation oncology system. Corrected to whole-word.

A word-boundary (\b) matcher would have failed silently on keywords with non-word edges: '$100,000' and '62%' drop to zero hits. The dataset authors such keywords in reasoning_must_include, so \b would have produced permanent false 'missing' violations. Lookarounds used instead.

Whole-word matching removes genuine true positives as well as false ones -- 'escalated', 'biologics', 'appropriately' no longer match their stems. Backfilled into the affected cases; 'denied'/'approval' deliberately not backfilled because a correct rationale can say 'should not be denied'.

fabrications remains a judge boolean by design -- the genuinely judgmental residue. It is narrowed by definition and counter-example, instrumented with provenance and a stability harness, and can still move without the system moving. That is stated rather than hidden.

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: GC-101/102/103 are duplicated across adult_complexity_cases.py and oncology_breadth_cases.py -- 108 case objects, 105 unique ids. Counters keyed by case_id are ambiguous for those three. The holdout is uncontaminated (all in-sample) but holdout.py's partition guard passes only because it compares id sets, not case objects. Needs its own change.
changes.why_this_component: The evaluator is the instrument every other number depends on. A metric that moves without the system moving is not a measurement, and it defeats audit: a reviewer asking 'how many hallucinations' got a number that differed between two runs of unchanged code.
changes.rollback_plan: Revert the chg-25 commits. No src/ file is touched and no schema changes, so the runtime is unaffected; the evaluator returns to a single judge-reported counter. The backfilled keyword variants in the case files would need reverting separately if the matcher reverts to substring.

verified_fixes: Lock hold 0.5095s to 0.0013s (SQLite) and 0.5436s to 0.0026s (Postgres); engine.pool.checkedout() == 0 during the LLM window, independently reproduced.
SQLite concurrent completions 1/10 to 10/10; Postgres 15/20 to 20/20 on a pool of 15; audit_write_failed 30 to 0 and 65 to 0.
Confirmed in the live clinical gate at merge HEAD: audit_write_failed 55 to 0, 'database is locked' 55 to 0, accuracy unchanged at 87.2%.
The duplicate-request_id contract holds identically on real Postgres 16, including the cross-patient 409 with no decision content in the body.
missed_fixes: A duplicate arriving while the first submission was in flight produced two decisions and then a permanent 500 for that request_id. The spec named two states where three existed. Fixed in the same iteration with an age-vs-agent_timeout heuristic and a decision lookup that cannot raise on multiplicity.
The resume path re-pinned a connection across the LLM call -- the exact defect the change removes, alive on one path. Fixed with a path-specific commit.
verified_risks: Keeping the injected session rather than a session factory was a deliberate deviation forced by a contradiction in the spec (a factory AND ~24 unmodified tests). It is materially equivalent on the normal path and was NOT on the resume path -- recorded as lessons L-032.
verdicts.notes: The in-flight heuristic is a heuristic, not a lease; a request exceeding agent_timeout is misclassified as dead. A claimed_at/worker_id lease and a UNIQUE constraint on authorization_decisions.request_id are the rigorous fixes and both need migrations.
